q.t: How many factors does 12 have?
q.k: len([d for d in range(1,13) if 12%d==0])

q.t: In idli-vada (idli on multiples of 3, vada on multiples of 5), what is the first number where you say 'idli-vada'?
q.e: The first number that is a multiple of both 3 and 5 is 15.

q.t: Is 17 a prime number?
o: Yes — its only factors are 1 and 17
q.e: A prime has exactly two factors. Nothing except 1 and 17 divides 17.

q.t: What is the smallest prime number?
q.e: 1 has only one factor so it isn't prime. 2 has exactly two: 1 and 2.

q.t: The number 1 is …
q.e: Prime needs exactly two factors, composite more than two; 1 has just one.

q.t: Which is the only even prime number?
q.e: Every other even number has 2 as an extra factor, so it has more than two factors.

q.t: Which number is divisible by 5?
q.e: A number is divisible by 5 when its last digit is 0 or 5.

q.t: Which number is divisible by 10?
q.e: Multiples of 10 always end in 0.

q.t: What is the third multiple of 7?
q.e: Count up in 7s: 7, 14, 21.

q.t: Jumpy jumps from 0 in steps of 4. Will he land on 24?
q.e: Steps of 4 land on 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24 — the multiples of 4.

q.t: Playing idli-vada (3 and 5) from 1 to 90, how many times is 'idli-vada' said?
q.e: Idli-vada comes on multiples of 15: 90 ÷ 15 = 6.

q.t: Playing idli-vada (3 and 5) from 1 to 90, how many times is 'idli' said (including idli-vada)?
q.e: Every multiple of 3 up to 90: 90 ÷ 3 = 30.

q.t: When is 'idli-vada' (3 and 5) said for the 10th time?
q.e: Idli-vada comes every 15 numbers, so the 10th is 10 × 15 = 150.

q.t: What are the common factors of 20 and 28?
How many prime numbers are there from 21 to 30?
q.k: len([n for n in range(21,31) if all(n%d for d in range(2,n))])
q.e: Only 23 and 29. The rest are even or multiples of 3 or 5 (21, 25, 27 …).

q.t: Which pair are twin primes?
q.e: Twin primes are primes that differ by 2. 43 and 47 differ by 4; 27 and 51 aren't prime.

q.t: Which of these is a prime number?
q.e: 51 = 3 × 17, 91 = 7 × 13, 57 = 3 × 19. Only 37 has no factors except 1 and itself.

q.t: Which pair is co-prime?
q.e: 18 = 2 × 3 × 3 and 35 = 5 × 7 share no prime. 30 & 415 share 5; 81 & 18 share 9; 15 & 39 share 3.

q.t: Is 8536 divisible by 4?
o: Yes — the last two digits 36 are a multiple of 4
q.e: Only the last two digits matter for 4, because 100 is a multiple of 4. 36 = 4 × 9.

q.t: What is the perfect number between 1 and 10?
q.e: Its factors 1 + 2 + 3 + 6 = 12, which is twice 6.

q.t: Treasures are on 28 and 70. What is the LARGEST jump size that reaches both?
q.e: Common factors of 28 and 70 are 1, 2, 7, 14. The largest is 14.

q.t: Find the prime factorisation of 104.
q.e: Keep halving: 104 → 52 → 26 → 13. Three 2s, then 13, which is prime.

q.t: A number's prime factorisation has one 2, two 3s and one 11. What is the number?
What is the smallest number whose prime factorisation has three different primes?
q.e: Use the three smallest primes: 2 × 3 × 5 = 30.

q.t: Which number is the product of exactly three different primes?
Is 225 divisible by 27?
o: No — 225 has only two 3s but 27 needs three
q.e: 225 = 3 × 3 × 5 × 5 and 27 = 3 × 3 × 3. You need enough copies of each prime.

q.t: What is the smallest number that is a multiple of every number from 1 to 10 except 7?
q.e: It needs 8 = 2×2×2, 9 = 3×3 and 5: 8 × 9 × 5 = 360. That covers 2, 3, 4, 6 and 10 automatically.

q.t: What is the smallest number that is a multiple of every number from 1 to 10?
q.e: Take 360 (everything except 7) and multiply by 7, since 360 has no 7 in it: 2520.

q.t: For a co-prime pair like 4 and 9, the first common multiple is …
q.e: With no shared factor, nothing can be saved, so the first common multiple is 4 × 9 = 36.

q.t: How many 3-digit primes can you make using each of 2, 4 and 5 once?
q.e: The last digit is 2 or 4 (even) or 5 (multiple of 5) — every arrangement has a factor besides 1 and itself.

q.t: 1955 is the product of three primes all less than 30. What is the largest of them?
What is the smallest number whose prime factorisation has four different primes?
Two numbers below 10 play idli-vada. The first idli-vada comes after 50 and before 60. What are they?
q.e: 7 and 8 share no factor, so their first common multiple is 56. 8 & 9 → 72; 6 & 9 → 18; 5 & 9 → 45.

q.t: How many leap years are there from 2024 to 2099?
q.k: len([y for y in range(2024,2100) if y%4==0])
q.e: 2024, 2028, …, 2096: (2096 − 2024) ÷ 4 + 1 = 19. No century year falls in the range.

q.t: What is the largest 4-digit palindrome divisible by 4?
q.k: max(i for i in range(1000,10000) if str(i)==str(i)[::-1] and i%4==0)
q.e: The last digit equals the first, so it must be even (≤ 8). 8998 fails (98 isn't a multiple of 4); 8888 works (88 = 4 × 22).

q.t: To check that 14560 is divisible by 2, 4, 5, 8 and 10, which TWO checks are enough?
q.e: Divisible by 8 means divisible by 2 and 4 too; 8 and 5 together give 2 × 5 = 10.

q.t: 10000 = A × B, and neither A nor B ends in 0. What is the larger of A and B?
q.e: 10000 = 2×2×2×2 × 5×5×5×5. Keep all 2s apart from all 5s: 16 × 625 (any 2 with a 5 makes a 10 and a final 0).

q.t: After 2 and 3, why is the number right after a prime always composite?
o: Every prime after 2 is odd, so the next number is even and bigger than 2
Because it is a multiple of 3
It isn't — it is sometimes prime
q.e: Even numbers bigger than 2 have 2 as an extra factor.

q.t: What is the remainder when 2345 is divided by 2? By 5? Give the remainder for 5.
q.e: 2345 ends in 5, so it's a multiple of 5 — remainder 0. (By 2 the remainder is 1 because it's odd.)

q.t: Which number is divisible by all of 2, 4, 5, 8 and 10?
q.e: 5600 ends in 0 (2, 5, 10) and its last three digits 600 = 8 × 75 (8, so 4). 572 and 2352 don't end in 0/5; 1250's last three digits 250 aren't a multiple of 8.
